stem: As soon as heparinized blood contacts the foreign surfaces of the pump-oxygenator, the coagulation, complement, kallikrein and fibrinolytic cascades respond. Activation of which plasma protein **may be the initial event** in activating these cascades?

choices.text: Plasminogen
Prekallikrein
Hageman factor (factor XII)
Fibrinogen
Complement components C3 and C5

explanation.text: Activation of **Hageman factor (factor XII)** may be the initial event in activating the coagulation, complement, kallikrein and fibrinolytic cascades; **platelets** appear to be activated **independently** at about the same time.

steps.text: Plasma contacts the foreign surfaces of tubing and pump-oxygenator, and air

explanation.text: The **greatest stimulus** to this humoral response is in the **oxygenator**, because gas exchange requires a large surface area. A process that is normally small, localized and often extravascular becomes a **massive intravascular** one.

explanation.title: Feedback loops
explanation.text: Kallikrein also activates Hageman factor and plasminogen. Once activated, the contact activation system **overcomes its normal regulating system**, and all the responses are amplified.
Activation of Hageman factor (factor XII) may be the initial event in activation of these cascades, although platelets appear to be independently activated at about the same time.
explanation.ref: Chapter 2: Hypothermia, Circulatory Arrest, and Cardiopulmonary Bypass, p. 51

choiceNotes.a: Plasminogen is converted to **plasmin** downstream (kallikrein facilitates this); it is not named as the initiating event.
choiceNotes.b: The kallikrein-bradykinin cascade is itself initiated by **contact activation of Hageman factor**.
choiceNotes.d: Fibrinogen is acted on by thrombin and binds the platelet GPIIb-IIIa receptor; it is not the initiating protein.
choiceNotes.e: Complement can be activated on contact with nonbiological surfaces **perhaps by way of Hageman factor**; C3 and C5 are downstream (C3a and C5a are its products).

Specific immune responses rapidly neutralize the products of the cascades

Platelets stay in their normally passive state until the end of bypass

Result

stem: Activation of the complement cascade during CPB produces the anaphylatoxins **C3a and C5a**. Which set of actions is attributed to them?

choices.text: Dilate arterioles, elicit pain, and convert plasminogen to plasmin
Inhibit platelet adhesion, aggregation, and secretion
Digest fibrin clots and thrombi in the circulation
Increase vascular permeability and mediate leukocyte chemotaxis
Regulate renal water excretion and raise systemic blood pressure

explanation.text: **C3a and C5a** increase vascular permeability, cause smooth muscle contraction, mediate leukocyte chemotaxis, and facilitate neutrophil aggregation and enzyme release.

explanation.title: Do not mix up with bradykinin
explanation.text: Bradykinin also increases vascular permeability and initiates smooth muscle contraction, but it also **dilates arterioles and elicits pain**; it comes from the **kallikrein** cascade, not from complement.

Adverse effects of complement activation relate to depletion of a component (complement) necessary for normal immune response and to adverse effects of the intravascular production of anaphylatoxins (C5a and C3a).
explanation.ref: Chapter 2: Hypothermia, Circulatory Arrest, and Cardiopulmonary Bypass, p. 55

choiceNotes.a: Dilating arterioles and eliciting pain are actions of **bradykinin**; activation of plasminogen is an action of **kallikrein**.
choiceNotes.b: Inhibition of platelet adhesion, aggregation and secretion is the effect of sufficient platelet **cAMP**.
choiceNotes.c: Digesting fibrin clots and thrombi is the basic function of **plasmin**.
choiceNotes.e: Regulating renal water excretion is the role of **vasopressin (ADH)**, whose infusion also raises blood pressure in vasoplegia.

stem: Which statement about the circulating platelet **count** after clinical CPB is correct?

choices.text: It falls to about 60% of baseline, unrelated to CPB duration
It falls mainly because platelets are sequestered in the liver
It falls mainly because shear stresses destroy circulating platelets
It falls less with membrane oxygenators than with bubble oxygenators
It returns to the prebypass value within the first postoperative hour

explanation.text: After CPB the platelet count is about **60%** of the prebypass value and **does not correlate with the duration** of CPB.

explanation.title: In vitro test circuits (corrected for dilution)

items: Hemodilution (larger fall in clinical CPB)
**Cardiotomy sucker systems** substantially reduce the count

stem: The same processes that activate platelets during CPB lead almost simultaneously to processes that **inhibit** them. Which inhibitory mechanism does the source describe?

choices.text: Complement desensitization of the platelet membrane

Exposure of GPIIb-IIIa receptors that bind circulating fibrinogen

stem: In sheep, a simple venovenous shunt produced no adverse effects on white blood cells, platelets or pulmonary artery pressure, but adding an **oxygenator** to the circuit did. What does this demonstrate?

choices.text: Complement activation depends mainly on how long blood circulates outside the body
Leukocyte and platelet losses result mainly from sequestration in the liver
Complement activation depends on blood in the boundary layer
Pulmonary hypertension results mainly from contact of blood with the circuit tubing
Infused complement-activated plasma cannot reproduce these changes

explanation.text: Only when an **oxygenator** was added did white cells and platelets fall and pulmonary artery pressure rise markedly: important complement activation depends on a large proportion of blood in the **boundary layer**.

steps.text: Increased alveolar-arterial O~2~ difference; pulmonary edema

explanation.text: Neutrophil-mediated **pulmonary endothelial injury** and increased lung vascular permeability, perhaps also mediated by reactive oxygen metabolites, may contribute to the adverse effects of CPB on pulmonary function.

stem: During routine, adequately heparinized CPB, which statement about the coagulation cascade is correct?

choices.text: Heparin blocks it incompletely, so small amounts of fibrin form
Heparin blocks it completely, so no fibrin forms until protamine reversal
Soluble factors fall severely and explain most later bleeding
Only the extrinsic phase is activated by the foreign surfaces

explanation.text: Heparin **largely but incompletely** inhibits coagulation during CPB, so small amounts of fibrin form even during routine CPB.
